title: 20 Money Myths That Keep You Poor
description:
Most money mistakes don't come from bad luck, they come from bad ideas that sound like common sense. In this video I break 20 money myths from three angles: the math (cash, houses, Social Security, tax refunds), the mindset (luck, budgets, frugality) and the playbook (credit cards, debt, investing).

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:14 How we got the numbers
1:40 Angle 1: The Numbers
1:43 1. Small amounts don't matter
3:12 2. Cash is the safest place
4:37 3. Your house is your best investment
6:02 4. Renting is throwing money away
7:22 5. Social Security will cover retirement
8:52 6. The tax refund is free money
10:05 7. You can time the market
11:26 Angle 2: The Psychology
11:33 8. More income will fix it
12:49 9. Rich people just got lucky
13:58 10. Budgets are for broke people
15:08 11. Talking about money is rude
16:19 12. I'm too young or too old
17:33 13. Frugal means cheap
18:39 14. Investing is gambling
19:56 A quick favor
20:09 Angle 3: The Playbook
20:15 15. Carry a balance to build credit
21:27 16. Checking your score hurts it
22:34 17. Close old cards to boost your score
23:41 18. All debt is bad
24:52 19. You need a lot to start investing
25:58 20. You need an expert to begin
27:08 Ten rules to replace the myths
28:03 How myths cost real money
29:23 Questions people ask
31:29 Recap: all 20 myths
32:13 What to do next

Sources:
- Social Security Administration: benefits replace about 40% of an average worker's pre-retirement earnings
- IRS Filing Season Statistics (average refund around $3,000 in recent seasons)
- Consumer Financial Protection Bureau: credit scores, soft vs hard inquiries, credit utilization; AnnualCreditReport.com
- Carlson, Kim, Lusardi and Camerer, Bankruptcy Rates among NFL Players with Short-Lived Income Spikes (NBER, 2015)
- Thomas J. Stanley and William D. Danko, The Millionaire Next Door (1996)
- Rule of 72, inflation and growth figures: stated illustrative math

Photos: Wikimedia Commons contributors. Full credits and licenses: https://github.com/ryan-rover-money-channel/ryan-rover-money/blob/main/agendamento/creditos/video42.md
